mlr3changepoint

Package website: sleepysnorlax05.github.io/mlr3changepoint

Weakly supervised changepoint detection for mlr3.

mlr3changepoint is the changepoint detection package of the mlr3 ecosystem. A changepoint or peak model needs a penalty that sets how many changes it keeps. The package learns that penalty for each sequence from labelled examples, as a function of features of the sequence. Its tasks, learners, predictions and measures work with resample(), benchmark(), mlr3tuning and mlr3pipelines.

The supervision is weak. Each label covers a region of a sequence and says how many changes it holds, for example 1change on positions 90 to 110 or 0changes on a flat stretch. A label does not give the position of a change or a value for each point. Changepoint labels follow penaltyLearning, and peak labels follow PeakError.

The package is developed during Google Summer of Code 2026, and its API may still change.

Feature overview

  • A "changepoint" task type, TaskCpt, holding one labelled sequence per row with "changepoint" or "peak" labels.
  • Four learners that predict a log(lambda) penalty per sequence from its features: linear interval regression, gradient boosted trees, and max margin interval trees and forests.
  • A featureless baseline that learns one constant penalty, for checking that the features help in benchmark().
  • Three measures that decode the segmentation each penalty selects and score it against the labels.
  • autoplot() methods that draw the labelled sequences, the predicted changes and the ROC curve.

Resources

The package website has a chapter on each part of the package and case studies on real and simulated data.

  • Start with Getting started for a first workflow from task to score.
  • Learn how tasks and labels describe sequences and labelled regions.
  • Compare the learners and their hyperparameters.

  • Follow the case studies on neuroblastoma copy-number profiles, peak detection in count data and a learner benchmark.

Installation

Install the development version from GitHub:

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("sleepysnorlax05/mlr3changepoint", dependencies = TRUE)

dependencies = TRUE also installs the solvers and regressors the learners use. The MMIT and MMIF learners need the mmit package, which is not on CRAN. Its upstream sources no longer compile on macOS and Windows, so pak installs a patched copy from sleepysnorlax05/mmit/Rpackage.

Learners

Key Label Packages
changepoint.intregrcv Cross-Validated Interval Regression penaltyLearning
changepoint.xgboost.aft Extreme Gradient Boosting AFT xgboost
changepoint.mmit Max Margin Interval Tree mmit
changepoint.mmif Max Margin Interval Forest mmit, future.apply
changepoint.featureless Featureless Constant Penalty penaltyLearning

Every learner also needs penaltyLearning and computes its model paths with changepoint for "changepoint" labels or PeakSegOptimal and PeakError for "peak" labels.

Measures

Key Label What it scores
changepoint.label_error Label Error Share of labelled regions with a false positive or false negative
changepoint.label_accuracy Label Accuracy One minus the label error
changepoint.auc Area Under the ROC Curve Area under the ROC curve traced by shifting all predicted penalties

Example

We simulate ten toy sequences. Odd ones change mean twice and carry a 1change label around each change. Even ones are flat and carry a 0changes label.

library(mlr3)
library(mlr3changepoint)
library(data.table)

set.seed(36)
signal = vector("list", 10L)
label = vector("list", 10L)
for (i in seq_len(10L)) {
  if (i %% 2L == 1L) {
    signal[[i]] = c(rnorm(100, 18), rnorm(100, 36), rnorm(100, 9))
    label[[i]] = data.table(start = c(90, 190), end = c(110, 210), label = "1change")
  } else {
    signal[[i]] = rnorm(100, 0)
    label[[i]] = data.table(start = 1, end = 100, label = "0changes")
  }
}

TaskCpt stores one sequence and its labels per row.

task = TaskCpt$new(
  id = "toy", backend = data.table(signal = signal, label = label),
  target = "label", sequence = "signal", label_type = "changepoint"
)

We train the interval regression learner and predict a log(lambda) for each sequence.

learner = lrn("changepoint.intregrcv", Kmax = 3L, n.folds = 2L, min.observations = 2L)
learner$train(task)
prediction = learner$predict(task)

The measures decode the segmentation each penalty selects and score it against the labels.

prediction$score(msrs(c("changepoint.label_error", "changepoint.auc")), task = task)
#> changepoint.label_error         changepoint.auc 
#>                       0                       1

autoplot() draws each sequence with its labelled regions and dashed lines at the predicted changes.

ggplot2::autoplot(prediction, task = task)

Bugs, questions, feedback

mlr3changepoint is free and open source software, and feedback is welcome. Report bugs, ask questions or suggest features in the issue tracker. A minimal reproducible example made with reprex makes a bug much easier to fix.

Related work

  • penaltyLearning: supervised penalty learning for changepoint detection, and the source of the labelled-region setup used here.
  • changepoint: classical changepoint methods. Its SegNeigh solver computes the changepoint model paths.
  • PeakSegOptimal and PeakError: optimal peak models and peak label errors, used for "peak" labels.
  • mmit: maximum margin interval trees and forests.
  • rupturesRcpp, binsegRcpp, fpop and dust: fast unsupervised segmentation.
